cards.front: Recall a key point about Exam Technique and Preparation
cards.back: Exam structure: 2 hours, 100 marks. Section A - Core Technical Principles (20 marks, short answer), Section B - Specialist Technical Principles (30 marks, short and extended), Section C - Designing and Making Principles (50 marks, extended response).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Exam Technique and Preparation
cards.back: Command words: 'State' - brief factual answer (1-2 marks). 'Describe' - say what happens (2-4 marks). 'Explain' - describe AND give reasons (3-6 marks). 'Evaluate' - give both sides and reach a justified conclusion (6-10 marks). 'Justify' - give reasons for your choice (4-6 marks).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Exam Technique and Preparation
cards.back: Time management: 2 hours for 100 marks = 1.2 minutes per mark. Section A: 24 minutes. Section B: 36 minutes. Section C: 60 minutes. Leave 10 minutes for checking.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Exam Technique and Preparation
cards.back: Section C strategy: this section tests AO3 most heavily - worth 50 marks. Read the context carefully, identify the user and their needs, use the SEE framework (Social, Economic, Environmental) for evaluation, always justify conclusions with specific evidence.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Exam Technique and Preparation
cards.back: Common errors: not reading the question carefully, vague answers without specific examples, writing everything you know instead of selecting relevant information, not evaluating (giving one side only), ignoring the command word.

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: Universal exam approach: 1) Read the question twice, identify the command word and topic, 2) Plan your answer structure (30 seconds), 3) Write using specialist vocabulary and specific examples, 4) For evaluation: present both sides, reach a justified conclusion, 5) Check your answer addresses the question asked.

cards.back: Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: In an exam, you should write everything you know about a topic to show the examiner how much you have revised. Correct: Examiners mark what is RELEVANT to the question, not how much you write. Writing everything you know wastes time and often misses the mark because you do not focus on what was asked. AQA D&T 8552: Written exam 50% + NEA 50%. AOs: AO1 Recall (20%), AO2 Apply (30%), AO3 Analyse & evaluate (50%). Section C tests all three AOs but focuses heavily on AO3. For grade 9, demonstrate perceptive evaluation, justified conclusions, fluent specialist vocabulary, and structured answers.

The AQA GCSE D&T written exam (8552/W) is worth 50% of the final grade, lasts 2 hours and carries 100 marks. Section A tests core technical principles (20 marks, short-response questions covering all topic areas). Command words determine the type of response required. 'State' or 'Name' requires a brief factual answer (1-2 marks). 'Describe' requires a detailed account of features or processes (2-4 marks). 'Explain' requires description plus reasoning (why something happens or why a choice is made) (3-6 marks). 'Analyse' requires breaking down a topic into components and examining relationships between them

cards.front: Revision Planning and Exam Day Strategy
cards.back: Effective GCSE D&T revision should begin at least 8 weeks before the exam and follow a structured plan. Week 1-2: review all notes, identify knowledge gaps using the specification checklist. Week 3-4: fill knowledge gaps using revision guides, BBC Bitesize and textbook notes. Week 5-6: practise applying knowledge to exam-style questions, focusing on AO2 and AO3 skills. Week 7-8: complete full past
